title: Stream-aware tool ledger + adaptive recursion guards for multi-tool chains
creator: Aisha Park
description: Background and problem: As we increase support for multi-tool / function-calling chains with streaming responses, we observe two classes of failures in production: (1) accidental infinite or deeply-recursive tool loops that blow out token budgets and GPU cycles; (2) inconsistent state when partial tool results are injected into the model mid-stream (race between model stream and async tool return). Both issues lead to cost spikes and incorrect outputs for customers using chained tool workflows (e.g., agent-like orchestrations, tool-assisted code edits, multi-hop retrieval + synthesis).
acceptance_criteria: Session-scoped tool ledger is persisted for the lifetime of a request and prevents duplicate tool invocations using watermark-based idempotency.
Streaming checkpoint markers allow safe partial-injection: runtime can inject/rollback injected results without corrupting the model's output stream.

Adaptive recursion guard enforces a configurable per-session recursion budget (depth + cumulative token cost) and returns structured fallback objects when budget exceeded (compatible with function-calling v2 schema).
Backpressure signals are surfaced to the client via SSE chunk metadata (status: queued, injected, rolled_back, throttled).
End-to-end tests cover: duplicated tool suppression, speculative injection + rollback, recursion-crossing threshold behaviors, and compatibility shim with function-calling v2 structured outputs.
